competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight markets leaned dollar-strong and mildly risk-off into a quiet Treasury tape, with investors parked ahead of Fed minutes while front-end funding futures marked a sharper path. The October 2028 policy-path terminal is 4.5825 percent, up 65 basis points on the day, and cash funding is still 3.93 percent. Euro finished the 17 November fix at 1.0989, down about 2 percent over five days and at the bottom of its one-year range, with sterling at 1.3191 and broad softness in the Australian and New Zealand dollars. Dollar-yen held 159.30. Commodities split: WTI is 86.01 and Brent is 93.14, gold is 3864, and copper at 5.976 is at a seven-month low. Equities were mixed, with the Nasdaq at 24328 and the Dow at 50759, while the volatility index at 22.91 sat above complacent readings. Geopolitics stayed elevated around Hormuz and Kuwait. Macro coverage is uneven in places; these cross-asset marks are the working set. Watch euro-area inflation today, Australia jobs tomorrow, and Canada retail sales plus Japan inflation on Thursday.

expression_memo.rationale: The SOFR strip is 35bp to 78bp above cash SOFR at 3.93, so a receive pays for hikes and a payer pays negative carry versus funding. No expression is put on.

carry-is-king.invalidation: Add risk only if a receive again clears live cash after this path, with the SOFR strip giving back the jump so the forward is a premium over funding again. A further rise in cash policy keeps the book flat.

causal.assumptions_right: The invalidation was correctly set as cash converging on the forward. Flattening before the 41.5bp jump kept the small gain.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The open gain versus the 3.00 entry was treated as evidence the cushion remained, even though cash had already risen toward the forward.
causal.causal_divergence: The mark versus entry stayed slightly favorable while the premium versus live cash went to nothing.
causal.future_implication: Do not receive the SOFR strip or reopen Canada March while those forwards sit on the new path. The next receive needs a forward that still clears live cash.
causal.observed_reality: The receive was closed at 2.96 after cash had been rising from 2.26 toward 2.995. March is now 2.965, up 41.5bp, so the path repriced after the exit.
causal.original_belief: March Canada received near 3.00 was positive carry while cash was near 2.26, and only a move in cash policy or oil-driven inflation delivering the priced hikes should have ended it.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With cash already migrating toward 2.995, holding for a further grind lower would have been short the new path with no remaining premium over funding.

postmortems.future_rule: Close a receive when live cash has converged to the forward even if the mark is still a few basis points through the entry, and do not reopen that contract after a same-week path reprice larger than 20 basis points.
postmortems.lesson: The cushion on a receive is live cash versus the forward. A mark still a few basis points through the entry can hide a cushion that cash has already closed.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The receive was coherent only while cash stayed well below the forward. By the exit, cash was heading toward 2.995 and 2.96 was the path itself. The later 41.5bp jump confirmed that invalidation.
postmortems.what_failed: A 4bp improvement from 3.00 to 2.96 was easy to treat as proof the carry was still intact. Live cash had already moved toward 2.995, so the premium over funding was gone while the mark was still slightly through the entry.
postmortems.what_worked: The Canada March receive was closed once cash had been rising from 2.26 toward 2.995, which was the stated cash-policy invalidation. The book was already flat when March printed 2.965, up 41.5bp, so the small gain from the 3.00 entry was kept.

carry-is-king.thesis: Stay flat. Cash SOFR is 3.93 against March SOFR at 4.545, up 61.5bp, so receiving the strip pays for hikes instead of earning a premium over funding. Canada March at 2.965 is up 41.5bp and no longer clears a cash rate that was already rising toward the old forward. Currency carry stays off while oil is 86 and 93 and VIX is 22.91.

expression_memo.rationale: The US hike path is already in the price, and nothing dated still has a level left to reprice. Size stays zero.

catalyst-junkie.invalidation: Standing aside ceases to be the trade if a front SOFR contract or the two-year is still cheap to the hike path and a minutes clock is actually printed, or if a foreign yield plus a same-day release time shows a gap the print can close.
catalyst-junkie.thesis: Stay flat. March SOFR at 4.545 and September at 4.710 have already jumped 61bp and 78bp, and the two-year at 4.80 already holds that hike path. Fed minutes have no printed clock. Australia jobs, Japan inflation, and Canada retail sales have dates but no priced gap in this freeze. Oil at 86 and 93 is not a new shock. There is no dated release that still has a level left to reprice.

expression_memo.rationale: Every listed break is either the euro short just harvested or a break close with no adverse daily-close level. The book stays flat.

chart-guy.invalidation: Size goes on only after a later daily close that still holds one listed break and that comes with an explicit adverse close beyond entry.

causal.assumptions_right: The tactical spot short matched the close-only downside path, and the stated horizon was the exit.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The fresh range break printed on the same close as the exit, so the horizon harvested the trade as the break appeared. That was a feature of the clock, not a failure of the rule.
causal.causal_divergence: Price was still below the invalidation when the horizon ended the trade. The stop never triggered.
causal.future_implication: The five-session rule stands. A later close is a new signal, not a revision of this exit, and selling the same break on the harvest day is a chase.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed on the fifth session with the fixing at 1.0989 still below 1.1195, after a decline from 1.11 to 1.10.
causal.original_belief: A five-session euro short entered on the downside close should exit on the fifth daily mark or on a close above the 20-day average at 1.1195.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Holding past the fifth session would have broken the stated rule even though the close was still valid.

postmortems.expression_assessment: A tactical spot euro short matched the close-only downside path, and the five-session mark was the exit that had been stated.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: The euro short ran from 1.11 to 1.10 and was closed on the declared five-session mark, with the close still below the booked invalidation at 1.1195. That was ordinary variance around a rule that did what it was written to do, and the original process remains sound.
postmortems.timing_assessment: The cover was on the declared five-session mark while 1.0989 was still below the booked daily-close invalidation at 1.1195. The horizon ended the trade and the stop did not.
postmortems.what_worked: The euro spot short followed the decline from 1.11 to 1.10, and the 17 November close at 1.0989 finished below the 20-day average, so the five-session direction was right.

chart-guy.thesis: Stay flat in G10 spot. The euro close at 1.0989 is a fresh downside break on the same fixing that finished the five-session short from 1.11 to 1.10, so selling euro again is a chase of a trade the horizon already harvested. Kiwi, Aussie-Canada, dollar-Norway, and dollar-Sweden are clean breaks, but this freeze gives only the break closes and no adverse daily close, so none is a complete five-session expression.

expression_memo.rationale: Euro-sterling at 0.8331 isolates euro cheapness versus sterling and cancels the dollar.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro-sterling at 0.8331 isolates euro cheapness versus sterling and cancels the dollar.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: No dated central-bank meeting is in the freeze. The edge is a snapback off the one-year extreme, and it is exhausted if the cross extends through 0.8331.
lifecycle.realization_logic: Euro-sterling lifts off the 0.8331 one-year extreme as the sterling premium versus the euro mean-reverts, with the dollar cancelled.

cross-merchant.invalidation: Close the long if euro-sterling extends through 0.8331 before any euro-positive impulse, or if a UK yield premium versus the euro-area ten-year at 3.35 explains the cheapness as carry.
cross-merchant.thesis: Buy 8 million euro-sterling. The cross is 0.8331, the bottom of its one-year range and near the bottom of five years, while oil at 86 and 93 is not a blow-off and copper at 5.976 is not a sterling impulse. Euro-sterling cancels the dollar, the 5.10 US ten-year, and cash funding, which a long euro or a short sterling would keep. Aussie-Canada stays shut on this oil tape, and Aussie-kiwi richness agrees with the kiwi's floor break.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the dollar-yen winner. At 159.30 a new 4 million long is the wrong dollar expression.

spot_candidate.rationale: Close the dollar-yen winner. At 159.30 a new 4 million long is the wrong dollar expression.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 10 million euro short. Spot 1.0989 is the fresh downside break and the extreme is still the trade.

spot_candidate.rationale: Hold the 10 million euro short. Spot 1.0989 is the fresh downside break and the extreme is still the trade.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 10 million dollar-franc long. Spot 0.8402 is the five-day extension and the position is still on its 0.8393 entry. Do not add a second extreme pair.

spot_candidate.rationale: Hold the 10 million dollar-franc long. Spot 0.8402 is the five-day extension and the position is still on its 0.8393 entry. Do not add a second extreme pair.

dollar-king.invalidation: The euro short fails if euro, sterling, the Australian dollar and the kiwi stabilize together. The franc long fails if euro reclaims the downside break and dollar-franc loses its five-day extension. Dollar-yen is closed, so it no longer has a live stop.
dollar-king.thesis: Close the 4 million dollar-yen winner and keep the 10 million euro short and the 10 million dollar-franc long. Euro at 1.0989 is a fresh downside break, down 2 percent in five days at the bottom of its one-year range, with the two-year at 4.80 and March SOFR at 4.545. Dollar-yen at 159.30 is a five-year extreme that is up only 0.7 percent in five days, and a fresh 4 million long at that print is not a trade to put on. Dollar-franc at 0.8402 is still the open extension off a 0.8393 entry.

rates_candidate.rationale: March SOFR at 4.545 jumped 61bp while cash is still 3.93. That jump is the hike reprice itself, so there is no failed move to receive.

expression_memo.rationale: The dollar-yen short is the fade that is set up. Receiving March SOFR has no failed break, and fading the fresh euro or kiwi breakdown runs into a live hike catalyst.

spot_candidate.rationale: Hold the 10 million short. Dollar-yen at 159.30 is a five-year 93rd percentile and the upside break that failed at 159.60 is still failed.

mean-reverter.invalidation: The short ends if dollar-yen reasserts the failed 20-day upside break. The original ten-day tactical horizon from the 159.60 entry still governs.
mean-reverter.thesis: Hold the 10 million dollar-yen short. At 159.30 it is a five-year extreme, the five-day gain is only 0.7 percent, and the failed 20-day upside break at the 159.60 entry is still the reversal that is set up. Euro at 1.0989 and kiwi at 0.5499 are one-day breakdowns while the 61bp March SOFR jump and today's euro-area inflation print are live, so those fades stay blocked.

expression_memo.rationale: Realized funding should print about the same as the strip from December at 4.285 to September at 4.710, and paying funding on shocked-risk capital at the post-move price does not clear that path.

funding_view.implication: Staying at the official cash fixing beats paying that fixing on shocked-risk capital. The post-jump strip is the funding path, and taking that price has no timed residual above the funding charge.
funding_view.sr3_forward_view: December at 4.285 rises through March at 4.545, already about 61bp above cash SOFR at 3.93, to September at 4.710. The October 2028 terminal at 4.5825 sits below that September peak.

no-trade-skeptic.invalidation: A trade becomes actionable when a still-ahead release has a printed clock and the two-year and ten-year move with the SOFR strip. This hold is invalidated if that confirmed path takes realized funding through the December-to-September strip, or if March gives back the 61bp day and the yield fix confirms the giveback.
no-trade-skeptic.thesis: Hold flat. March SOFR at 4.545 is already 61bp above the 3.93 fixing, September is 4.710, and the October 2028 terminal at 4.5825 sits below that peak. Realized funding over this horizon should print about the same as that strip, so staying in cash beats paying funding on shocked-risk capital to own the post-move price. The two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10 did not show a comparable one-day story, and the dollar extremes are prints after the move rather than before it.

rates_candidate.rationale: The ten-year at 5.10 still yields a premium over the two-year and over the October 2028 terminal at 4.5825.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the ten-year. The front-end receive fades a hike path cash has not delivered, and the commodity-currency short is inferior because the dollar is already stretched.

spot_candidate.rationale: Short Australian dollar at 0.6735 tracks weak copper, but the dollar is already extended and oil headlines can bounce commodity currencies.

perma-bear.invalidation: Cover the ten-year if the yield moves back through the 5.24 entry. That is a further selloff from tighter policy and higher term premium with no growth break.
perma-bear.thesis: Hold the 3.125 million US ten-year receive. The yield is 5.10, 14 basis points through the 5.24 entry, while cash SOFR is 3.93 and March SOFR has jumped to 4.545. Copper at 5.976 is a seven-month low and the ten-year still yields about 30 basis points over the 4.80 two-year, so 5.10 still pays for a slowdown. Receiving the front end would fade hikes that cash has not delivered, and paying it would chase the one-day jump.

rates_candidate.rationale: September SOFR at 4.710 is the receive that replaces a delivered Australian bill pay.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 35 million Australian March 2027 bill short. The bill is 5.00 versus a 4.80 entry, oil has left the scare zone, and keeping the pay would chase a hike that has already been marked.

spot_candidate.rationale: The Australian dollar long is the cyclical leg already on the book.

rates_candidate.rationale: The fade of the hike overshoot belongs in September at 4.710, not in a late March pay.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 50 million March SOFR short. Live March is 4.545 versus a 4.52 entry after a 61.5bp day, so the short is a late pay with the hike already in the strip.

spot_candidate.rationale: The Australian dollar long is not a reason to stay short March SOFR.

rates_candidate.rationale: New money belongs in the September receive, not in a larger Australian-dollar line.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 15 million Australian-dollar long. The drawdown is about 22 pips and dollar pessimism is already extreme. Size stays unchanged.

spot_candidate.rationale: Hold the 15 million long. Spot is 0.6735 versus entry 0.6757, a mixed technical picture, with copper still at 5.976.

rates_candidate.rationale: Receive September 2027 SOFR at 4.710, the peak of the strip after a 78bp day, with cash SOFR at 3.93.

cross_market_rv.rationale: Canada and Australia moved less, and no spread history makes a cross-market package cleaner than the US September receive.

curve.rationale: The two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10 imply a modest positive slope. The dislocation is the outright September jump.

five_year.rationale: No five-year yield is in the freeze.

rates_tenor_scan.selection_rationale: September 2027 is the peak of the strip and the largest one-day hike print.

stir_policy_path.rationale: Receive September 2027 SOFR at 4.710. It is up 78bp on the day, the peak of the strip, with cash SOFR at 3.93 and the October 2028 terminal at 4.5825. Oil at 86.01 and 93.14 leaves that one-session hike cycle as the overshoot.

ten_year.rationale: The ten-year is 5.10. The shock that can be faded is in the front end, not term premium.

two_year.rationale: The two-year at 4.80 is the cash twin of the hike overshoot, but its day change is not in the freeze, so the measured print is the September contract.

expression_memo.rationale: September is the cleaner expression of a printed hike-cycle overshoot than adding to a mixed Australian-dollar slide.

spot_candidate.rationale: The existing Australian-dollar long is the cyclical hold. New risk goes to the SOFR hump.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The strip fails to extend beyond September at 4.710 and March at 4.545.
lifecycle.realization_logic: September SOFR gives back a material part of the 78bp jump while oil stays near 86 and 93.

perma-bull.invalidation: The September receive is invalidated if that contract holds 4.710 and the strip pushes further, or if oil moves back toward the prior scare zone. The Australian-dollar hold is invalidated if spot fails to stabilize while March SOFR at 4.545 and September at 4.710 hold the repricing.
perma-bull.thesis: Close the Australian bill pay and the March SOFR pay, hold the 15 million Australian-dollar long, and receive 20 million of September 2027 SOFR. Cash SOFR is 3.93 while September is 4.710 after a 78bp jump, and oil is 86 and 93 rather than the old scare zone, so the pro-growth expression is that the one-session hike cycle was too much. The Australian dollar at 0.6735 is only a small drawdown from 0.6757 and stays as the cyclical long. The receive fails if September holds 4.710 and extends, or if oil returns to the scare zone.

rates_candidate.rationale: March SOFR at 4.545 is the public hike reprice. Paying it joins that story, and receiving it has no current futures net behind it.

expression_memo.rationale: The existing dollar-yen short is the position already on, and the dollar long is still the larger crowd. A new bill-strip pay joins the public hike story.

spot_candidate.rationale: Keep the existing 10 million short from 159.60. Freeze spot is 159.30. This is the crowded anti-dollar bet and it is not increased.

positioning-cynic.invalidation: The fade is exhausted by a sustained hold above 159.60, which would show the dollar long being rebuilt. The freeze spot is 159.30, so that adverse level has not printed.
positioning-cynic.thesis: Hold the 10 million dollar-yen short and do not add. The larger crowd is still the dollar long, with euro at 1.0989 and kiwi at 0.5499 on the floor, but this short is itself the crowded anti-dollar bet because more than one seat is already short dollar-yen from nearby levels. March SOFR at 4.545, up 61bp, is the public hike story and is left alone. No fresh futures net is available, so a receive is not opened on the reprice alone.

rates_candidate.rationale: The 2027 Canada strip is the receive that fades today's hike mark, and copper at 5.976 says that path is too fast to deliver in full.

expression_memo.rationale: Keep a smaller Canada receive because the one-day hike marks are the overshoot, and take half off because oil at 93 revives energy pass-through.

spot_candidate.rationale: Australian dollar at 0.6735 sits on the same copper low but mixes the policy disagreement with commodity beta.

rate-dove.invalidation: The residual dies if the 2027 Canada strip is marked through the 3.40 entry into the mid-3s, or if today's euro-area inflation print or tomorrow's Australia jobs report extends the March selloff instead of stalling it.
rate-dove.thesis: Cut the Canada 2027 strip receive in half, leaving 21.25 million. March Canada rose 41.5bp to 2.965 and March US SOFR rose 61.5bp to 4.545 in the same session, which is too fast to own at full size against copper at a seven-month low of 5.976. Brent at 93.14 puts energy pass-through back into the Canada strip, so full size is no longer the receive. The known 2027 contracts are still below a mid-3s path, so the other half stays.

rates_candidate.rationale: December at 4.285 is 35bp over cash and already holds the near-dated hike.

expression_memo.rationale: Cover the December short. The 17bp gain from 4.115 is the priced part of the path, and the residual belongs in September.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-yen at 159.30 is a weaker expression of a hike that is already in the December contract.

rates_candidate.rationale: September at 4.710 is still about 22bp short of a four-hike level near 4.93, with only a few basis points over June at 4.675.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the September short. The freeze at 4.710 is slightly through the 4.755 entry, and that residual is the hawkish gap rather than a reason to cover.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-yen is not cleaner than this short for the residual fourth hike.

rate-hawk.invalidation: The September short changes if that contract falls to the June price of 4.675, which would mark the peak as passed and the fourth hike as rejected. December stays covered unless the hike comes back out of a contract that already prices it.

causal.assumptions_right: A true hiking cycle, as distinct from removing one cut, was the only path that could pay the short.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The oil pair used as the invalidation did not describe the oil market that traded, and there was no exit tied to the Canada path itself.
causal.causal_divergence: Brent could stay near 93 while the forward moved toward easier policy, so the oil premise and the rate path diverged.
causal.future_implication: Do not re-short Canada March at 2.965 to replay the 3.12 entry, and do not replace it with an Australian bill pay on a strip that is flat at the front and lower in the back.
causal.observed_reality: The contract fell from 3.12 to 2.96, a loss, while oil is now 86 and 93 rather than 105. The later print at 2.965 did not rebuild a hiking cycle.
causal.original_belief: A short Canada March future at 3.12 would pay if firmer oil forced a hiking cycle rather than merely removing one priced cut.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: An exit when the Canada forward itself fell, rather than when oil revisited 105, would have recognized that the hiking cycle was not being delivered.

postmortems.expression_assessment: The invalidation lived in the oil market rather than in the forward being shorted. Brent near 93 could not keep the short right once the contract had dropped and there was no rule that closed it when the Canada path itself eased.
postmortems.future_rule: Invalidate a short-rate position on that contract's own path. If the forward falls and the strip is not pricing hikes, the hiking-cycle thesis is finished even when Brent is still in the low 90s. Do not pay Australian bills when the front is 5.00 and the back is 4.88.
postmortems.lesson: The position was the Canada forward, and that forward fell from 3.12 to 2.96. Oil near 105 was a stale premise and left the hawkish rethink without a rate path.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The thesis treated firmer oil as the opening of a Canadian hiking cycle. From 3.12 to 2.96 the forward added easing. Shedding one priced cut and starting a hiking cycle are different paths, and this short was paid only by the second.
postmortems.what_failed: The Canada March short from 3.12 to 2.96 lost 16bp. The invalidation named oil near 105 and 93 and a hawkish rethink. Oil is now 86 and 93, so the 105 premise was stale, and the contract fell anyway.

rate-hawk.thesis: Cover the 10 million December SOFR short and hold the 12.5 million September SOFR short. December at 4.285 already holds the near-dated hike versus cash at 3.93 and is 17bp through the 4.115 entry, so that part of the path has been paid. September at 4.710 is the strip peak and is still short of a four-hike destination near 4.93, which is the residual hawkish gap. Australian bills are 5.00 at the front and 4.88 in the back, so they are not a fresh hiking cycle to pay.

expression_memo.rationale: Exit the dollar-yen long. It is not a fresh break, and the higher-policy-path trend is carried in the March pay.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro at 1.0989 is the clean spot dollar breakdown, but the policy-path contract is the trend itself.

rates_candidate.rationale: Pay March at 4.545 after a 61.5bp rise aligned with the two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10.

cross_market_rv.rationale: The live trend is the US path itself.

curve.rationale: The slope from 4.80 to 5.10 is about 30bp and no curve change is shown.

stir_policy_path.rationale: Pay March 2027 SOFR at 4.545 after a 61.5bp rise aligned with the two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10.

ten_year.rationale: The ten-year is 5.10 and no fresh ten-year change is shown.

two_year.rationale: The two-year at 4.80 confirms the direction, but no two-year change is in the freeze.

expression_memo.rationale: Pay 25 million of March SOFR. March, the two-year, and the ten-year are aligned higher.

spot_candidate.rationale: Short euro would ride the break to 1.0989. The cleaner continuation is the policy-path contract that just repriced.

lesson_considerations.rationale: March is the contract printing higher with the two-year and the ten-year, so the new pay is the confirming tenor rather than an add to a laggard that has stopped confirming.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The edge is exhausted if March gives back the day's rise or splits from the two-year and the ten-year.
lifecycle.realization_logic: The pay is marked in implied-rate space and profits while March implied keeps rising with the two-year and the ten-year.

trend-follower.invalidation: Cover the March pay if March implied stops rising together with the two-year and the ten-year, or if March gives back the day's 61.5bp reprice. A September print that keeps extending while March stalls would move the pay to September.
trend-follower.thesis: Close the 10 million dollar-yen long and pay 25 million of March 2027 SOFR. Dollar-yen at 159.30 is only slightly ahead of the 159.23 entry and the five-day rise is 0.7 percent, so that momentum has stalled. The live trend is the higher US policy path: March implied is 4.545, up 61.5bp, with the two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10.

rates_candidate.rationale: The US two-year at 4.80 is 87bp over cash SOFR at 3.93. That gap is the priced hiking path, not a cheap receive, and foreign cash rates needed to screen cross-market spreads are absent.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the euro-sterling long at 5 million. No rates expression clears a cash screen, and a new dollar short waits until the euro-dollar break stops extending.

spot_candidate.rationale: The owned long at 0.8331 is the value expression: a one-year floor with both legs already cheap versus the dollar.

value-guy.invalidation: The long is disproved if the one-year floor gives way as a euro-specific break that sterling does not match against the dollar. Twelve pips under the entry is not that event.
value-guy.thesis: Hold the 5 million euro-sterling long. The cross is 0.8331, 12 pips under the 0.8343 entry, at the bottom of its one-year range and near the bottom of five years. Both the euro and sterling are already cheap against the dollar, so the cross is the residual dislocation. Euro-dollar at 1.0989 is still breaking, so a new euro buy waits. The front end is rich to cash because hikes are priced, and that is not a value receive.

expression_memo.rationale: Option premium is not in the freeze, so convexity cannot be bought today. Selling the dollar extreme in spot would be a linear risk that is not being put on without a price.

vol-convexity.invalidation: This flat hold ends when a later set of marks quotes an option premium, implied volatility, and a strike that can be marked. A further spot print does not by itself supply that premium.
vol-convexity.thesis: Hold flat. Euro at 1.0989 is breaking down, kiwi at 0.5499 is on a five-year floor, and March SOFR is 4.545 after a 61bp up day, so the shape that fits is bounded optionality. The freeze has no option price, no implied volatility, and no strike. Convexity cannot be bought today, and selling the dollar extreme in spot would be a linear risk that is not being put on without a price.

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: Official cash funding is the zero-alpha benchmark. A trade must clear that cost on shocked risk capital with room rather than restate a move that has already printed.

A receive needs that contract to rally enough to cover cash funding on the capital at risk and still leave room. Oil and the volatility index keep the higher-rate path live, so the expected improvement does not clear.

candidate_assessments.rationale: Euro-sterling at 0.8331 has a live mark and no catalyst or carry that would lift a long above cash funding on the capital employed. With no expected drift over funding, the long does not clear.

deployment_hurdle.chosen_action_rationale: All three markable candidates fail to beat cash funding on shocked risk capital with room, so the flat book holds and takes no new risk.

grinder.invalidation: A later mark that shows a still-open gap versus a plausible funding path, wide enough to cover the cash fixing on the capital at risk with room, would end this flat stance.

opportunity_scan.rationale: Paying March restates a finished 61.5bp up day.
Receiving September fades a live higher-rate path while the contract sits only a little over March.
Spot 0.8331 is markable and offers no carry that would beat cash on a long.

grinder.thesis: The book stays flat. March funding futures at 4.545 have already repriced 61 basis points above the 3.93 cash fixing, September at 4.710 is only a little beyond that front contract, and euro-sterling at 0.8331 has no catalyst that would out-earn cash charged on risk capital. Preservation means declining new risk whose expected mark change does not clear that funding cost with room.

pragmatist.invalidation: The close is early if Canada March settles back through 2.70 while March funding futures hold near 4.545, which would show the jump as a one-session spillover. A move through 3.13 confirms the exit.

Paying March joins a move that has already printed.
Receiving September adds front-end duration in the same direction as the line being closed.
Euro-sterling at 0.8331 does not change the Canada front-end path.

candidate_interactions.rationale: A September receive adds front-end duration beside the Canada March receive.
A March pay offsets the long-duration beta of the Canada receive, but only by opening a second rates ticket.
Euro-sterling does not map onto the Canada March path.

portfolio_construction.chosen_actions_rationale: Close the Canada March receive and stop. The leftover gap to entry is smaller than the session that just printed, and the US contracts show the same move. A new pay or receive would be a second ticket. Cash at the official fixing is the holding.
portfolio_construction.existing_book_summary: One line: a long Canada March 2027 receive of 150 million, entry 3.13, freeze 2.965 after a 41.5 basis point session. The contract is still through the entry, and the leftover gap is smaller than the bar that just printed. No other position is on this book.

independent_handoff_opportunities.rationale: A 20 million September receive at 4.710 after a 78bp jump is markable new front-end duration.
A 25 million March pay at 4.545 after a 61.5bp jump is markable new payer risk.
An 8 million euro-sterling long at 0.8331 is a markable spot cross, separate from the rates book.

Paying March overlays a new rates ticket on a move that has already printed.
Euro-sterling does not change the front-end path and adds a second market.

pragmatist.thesis: Close the Canada March receive. The freeze is 2.965 versus a 3.13 entry, so the line is still through entry, but today's 41.5 basis point jump is larger than the 16.5 basis points left back to that entry. March funding futures rose 61.5 basis points and September rose 78. The residual is smaller than the session that just printed, so the receive comes off and no new rates ticket is added.

swinger.invalidation: The close is wrong if March implied trades back through 4.615 while crude is rising again and the two-year is still near 4.80.

opportunity_scan.rationale: Adding to the pay was considered. Entry 4.615 versus a 4.545 freeze is a decline that has already gone through the position.
September at 4.710 is the hump above the October 2028 terminal. A receive was considered and rejected because the two-year at 4.80 and the ten-year at 5.10 do not confirm a lower path.
Euro-sterling at 0.8331 is being bought in small size. That is not a dislocation worth a concentrated fade.

swinger.thesis: Close the March 2027 pay. The freeze is 4.545, through the 4.615 entry, and March now sits a few basis points under the October 2028 terminal at 4.5825. Oil is 86 and 93, not the prior spike, and a stall after that decline is not a reason to keep the full short. A small new March pay elsewhere does not validate the existing size. The March short comes off, and no replacement is opened.
